summary: Wilton sprawls across 29 square miles of Sacramento County's southern flatland — yet holds barely 6,200 people, giving it a density of just 214 per square mile, which is closer to genuine ranchland than anything resembling suburbia. The terrain is open-sky valley floor: irrigated pastures, horse properties on multi-acre lots, and long sight lines toward the Sierra Nevada foothills to the east. With a median household income of nearly $172,000 and a median home price above $891,000, the price-to-income ratio sits around 5.2 — manageable by Sacramento-metro standards but firmly requiring dual high-earning salaries, and almost nothing here rents because the housing stock is overwhelmingly owner-occupied on large parcels. This is a textbook bedroom community; employment means commuting north into Elk Grove or Sacramento proper, roughly 20–30 minutes on surface roads like Grant Line Road, since no freeway cuts through town. Daily life reflects that rural pacing — there is no downtown, no walkable commercial strip, and retail or dining requires driving out to Elk Grove. What you get instead is 9.5 hours of daily sunshine, a 5.4% poverty rate, and the kind of quiet where the evening soundtrack is irrigation pumps and red-tailed hawks. Wilton is essentially a place people choose precisely *because* nothing is nearby — the tradeoff between seclusion and convenience is not a side effect but the entire premise.
